Definition: an oak or other strong tree
BiblicalUsage: ʼêlâh means an oak or other strong tree. In Genesis 35:4, the text says "and Jacob hid them under the oak which [was] by Shechem." In Judges 6:11, the text says "and sat under an oak which [was] in Ophrah."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: ʼêlâh tells me that creation is God's handiwork, and it still speaks of Him to anyone willing to look. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Gideon's Victory over Midian; God Blesses Jacob at Bethel; The Man of God from Judah
